brief: The CBK/BQK rule-making layer for Kosovo banking is highly centralised and, on paper, well published: a single legal-framework hub (bqk-kos.org/korniza-ligjore) carrying laws, regulations, rules, guidelines, orders and an archive; a dated PDF repository under /wp-content/uploads/YYYY/MM/ holding the binding texts; a per-meeting Board-decisions stream that is the earliest reliable adoption signal; and a supervision/licensing subtree covering the licensing manual, risk-based supervision manual and macroprudential measures. Everything is trilingual via a ?lang= parameter but with divergent sq/sr URL slugs, so a single-language crawl will under-collect. Two practical obstacles dominate: the whole domain returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt in this pass (bot defence, not a dead site — pages are freshly indexed, including June 2026 posts), and no standing public-consultation index for BQK drafts could be found in either sq or sr, with the only consultation evidence buried inside a document's own history. Consequently, consultation and deadline tracking should be built on the news stream, the Board-decision posts, the Official Gazette (which carries the enabling laws, notably the new Law 08/L-304 on Banks gazetted 27 January 2026), and full-text extraction of 'hyn në fuqi' / 'stupa na snagu' clauses from the PDFs themselves.
